categories.main_business_segments: Beijing Highlander Digital Technology Co., Ltd. primarily operates in three main business segments: intelligent navigation for ships, marine observation and detection equipment, and underwater data centers (UDC). The company provides integrated smart maritime solutions including ship intelligent navigation systems, composite radar systems, engine automation, and ship-shore integrated communication systems. It also develops deep-sea engineering equipment and services, and commercial underwater data centers that leverage marine renewable energy.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced technologies such as solid-state radar with Doppler processing, integrated navigation systems certified by international classification societies, and underwater data center technologies involving high-pressure sealing, corrosion resistance, and seawater cooling. It develops atmospheric diving suits, underwater observation networks, and intelligent marine monitoring platforms. The UDC integrates marine power supply, cooling, and remote monitoring technologies, and the company is pioneering the integration of offshore wind power with underwater data centers for green computing.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include oceanographic research institutions, telecommunications operators, offshore wind power operators, internet companies, and third-party IDC providers. The company serves maritime sectors including ocean shipping, coastal and inland waterways, national defense, marine disaster prevention, and marine scientific research. Its markets span domestic Chinese regions and international locations, with products applied in marine disaster prevention, intelligent shipping, and digital economy infrastructure.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in China, with significant activities in Beijing, Hainan (notably the free trade port in Hainan), Shanghai, Guangdong, Shandong, and other coastal provinces. It has established R&D and service networks in Canada, Germany, and Russia, and subsidiaries in Hong Kong and Germany, supporting global marine and maritime technology markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Beijing Highlander operates mainly in the midstream and downstream segments of the marine technology and digital infrastructure supply chain. It designs, manufactures, and integrates marine observation equipment, intelligent ship systems, and underwater data centers, providing end-to-end solutions including installation, operation, and maintenance services. The company also engages in technology development and system integration, positioning itself as a key technology provider and service operator.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company emphasizes innovation in AI-enabled intelligent navigation, marine disaster prevention, and underwater data center technologies. It focuses on developing solid-state radar, autonomous navigation, and integrated ship-shore communication systems aligned with new intelligent ship standards. R&D priorities include enhancing marine observation system intelligence, deep-sea equipment reliability, and green computing through offshore wind power integration. The company invests heavily in proprietary technology development and aims to lead in marine digital infrastructure and smart shipping.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through product sales of marine observation equipment, intelligent ship systems, and underwater data centers. The company also earns income from technical services, system integration, equipment leasing, and maintenance contracts. It engages in direct sales and distribution channels, with a significant portion of revenue from domestic customers and a growing share from international markets. Additionally, the company receives government subsidies and investment income related to its technology projects.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Beijing Highlander is positioned as a leading domestic player in marine technology and underwater data centers, holding a pioneering role in China’s marine digital infrastructure. It competes with other marine equipment manufacturers and technology providers but distinguishes itself through proprietary technologies, international certifications, and integration of green energy with data centers. The company has achieved significant breakthroughs in solid-state radar and underwater data center technologies, establishing a competitive edge in intelligent shipping and marine observation sectors.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, the company reported operating revenue of approximately RMB 383.9 million, a 49.06% decrease from the previous year, mainly due to project timing and strategic focus on high-margin orders. Net profit attributable to shareholders was RMB 8.2 million, a significant turnaround from prior losses. Total assets stood at about RMB 2.44 billion, with a slight increase year-over-year. The company continues to invest heavily in R&D, with expenditures reaching RMB 86.4 million, representing 22.51% of revenue, reflecting a growth-oriented and innovation-driven profile.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company offers unique value through its integration of advanced marine technologies, such as AI-powered intelligent navigation systems, solid-state radar with international certifications, and energy-efficient underwater data centers cooled by seawater and powered by offshore wind. Its solutions emphasize green, reliable, and cost-effective digital infrastructure for marine and shipping industries. The company’s comprehensive system integration capabilities, proprietary core technologies, and strategic alignment with national marine and digital economy policies differentiate it from competitors, providing customers with cutting-edge, sustainable, and secure marine technology solutions.
